The top row shows market-wide totals: total crypto market cap, BTC dominance and all-market volume from CoinGecko; open interest, perp volume, average funding, breadth and liquidations summed over the tracked coins. A green dot means the figure is live. Below it, data is combined from Binance, Bybit, OKX and Bitget USDT perpetuals. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index from Alternative.me runs from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed) and updates once a day. It combines volatility, market momentum and volume, social media, Bitcoin dominance and search trends. The dashboard checks for a new reading every 10 minutes.

A trade counts as whale-size at $500K or more for BTC and ETH, $250K for BNB and SOL, and $100K for the other coins, with a pop-up alert at $3M or more. Market Status cards, laid out like CoinMarketCap's homepage. Market Cap: total crypto market cap and 24h volume from CoinGecko; the line under it builds up while the page is open (one point a minute). Fear & Greed: Alternative.me's index on a five-zone gauge. Altcoin Season Index: the share of CoinGecko's top 100 coins (stablecoins left out) that beat Bitcoin over the last 30 days; 75 or more is Altcoin Season, 25 or less Bitcoin Season. CoinMarketCap's own index uses 90 days, which CoinGecko's free data doesn't offer, so the numbers won't match exactly. Average Crypto RSI: the average 14-day RSI of your coins from daily candles, with counts of overbought (70+) and oversold (30 or less) coins. Dominance: Bitcoin and Ethereum shares of total market cap from CoinGecko.

Sectors & Supply

LOADINGSelect a box to open it in its own window
T1

Sector Rotation

LOADING
How it works. Each candle is a sector: a green candle rising from the zero line is net inflow, a red candle falling below it is net outflow, and its height and label are that net flow in dollars. Net inflow is measured from the trades themselves: for each sector's 8 largest coins (CoinGecko's category lists, stablecoins left out), the dashboard adds up the last 24 hourly candles on Binance spot (Binance.US where Binance is blocked) and Binance USDT perpetual futures, which record how much was bought by takers — traders who pay the market price — and subtracts what takers sold. More aggressive buying than selling is money coming in; the buy share is market buys ÷ all volume. This is a better read of real buying and selling than the change in market cap, which mostly reflects price moves. The 24h % is CoinGecko's change in the sector's market cap. Refreshed every 10 minutes. A coin Binance doesn't list is skipped, and if no taker data loads at all (Binance blocks some regions), the candles fall back to the market-cap change and say so. When nothing loads at all, the panel says NO DATA and stays empty.
E

Ecosystems

LOADING
How it works. Each candle is a blockchain ecosystem (CoinGecko's ecosystem lists: Solana, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Base, Sui and more): a green candle rising from the zero line is net inflow over the last 24 hours, a red candle falling below it is net outflow. It is measured the same way as T1: for each ecosystem's 8 largest coins (stablecoins and wrapped coins left out) the dashboard adds up the last 24 hourly candles on Binance spot (Binance.US where Binance is blocked) and Binance USDT perpetuals, taking what takers bought minus what they sold. Coins that sit in several ecosystems count in each. The 24h % is CoinGecko's change in the ecosystem's market cap. Refreshed every 10 minutes; when nothing loads the panel says NO DATA instead of showing made-up flows.

          How it works. On-chain sector data comes from DefiLlama's free public API (no key), which reads smart-contract balances on more than 400 blockchains. Sectors are DefiLlama's protocol categories (lending, DEXs, liquid staking, restaking, bridges, RWA, yield, derivatives and more): TVL is the value of tokens locked in each sector's contracts, and the 1-day and 7-day changes are the change in that value, which includes price moves as well as deposits and withdrawals. Fees are what users paid each sector's protocols in the last 24 hours, and DEX volume is on-chain swap volume. Chains shows TVL by blockchain and how many protocols run on it. Stablecoins shows the supply of every USD stablecoin: new supply minted is fresh money entering crypto, and supply burned is money leaving, which is the closest free measure of real inflow. Select a row for its largest protocols or chains. Refreshed every 15 minutes.             Whale · Shark · Dolphin · Shrimp Volume

            WAITING
            How it works. Every trade the dashboard receives live — Binance spot and perpetuals, Bybit and OKX perpetuals, and Coinbase spot — is sorted by its size. Exchanges don't show who owns how much, so holdings (the 1%–10% of supply that defines a whale holder) can't be seen from trades; instead the whale tier is set from the coin's own supply: a single trade worth at least 0.001% of the coin's circulating market value (CoinGecko), and never less than the dashboard's whale-trade size ($500K for BTC and ETH, $250K for BNB and SOL, $100K for others). Sharks trade at least a tenth of the whale size, dolphins at least a hundredth, and shrimp are everything smaller. The chart is drawn with TradingView's open-source Lightweight Charts: the top is the coin's price candles from the exchange (Binance or Bybit, then OKX, Coinbase or Kraken), and under it are four volume panes, one per tier. Each bar is the dollar volume that tier traded in that candle; green when the tier bought more than it sold, red when it sold more, and the brighter the bar the more one-sided it was. Move across the chart to read each tier's buys, sells and net for that candle. History is kept on this computer — 1-minute candles for the last 7 days and 15-minute candles for good — and only covers the time the dashboard has been open. Hover for each tier's buys, sells and net.

                    Ethplorer key (free, optional backup)
                    Blockscout is used first and needs no key. Ethplorer is the backup for Ethereum tokens: its shared key returns only the top 100 holders, a free personal key from ethplorer.io returns the top 1,000. Paste it here (never in chat); it stays on this computer and is sent only to Ethplorer.
                    Smart money data, for the coin selected in the chart. Top traders: the long share of positions held by Binance's top 20% of futures accounts by margin balance (OKX's top-trader ratio where Binance doesn't list the coin) — the closest free, live measure of what large, well-funded traders are doing. Crowd: the long share of all Binance accounts (Bybit where Binance doesn't list it). The gap between them shows whether big traders lean against the crowd. Taker buy/sell: Binance futures market-buy volume divided by market-sell volume (OKX where Binance doesn't list the coin) over the window you pick — 5, 15 or 30 minutes, 1, 4, 12 or 24 hours, or 7, 14 or 30 days — or Match chart, which follows the chart's timeframe (1m uses 5 minutes, Day uses 24 hours, Week 7 days, 2 Week 14 days). Above 1 means buyers are more aggressive; "prev" is the same length of time just before. Exchanges keep about 30 days of this history. For screen readers, each tile reads as one sentence, and the summary is announced only when its meaning changes, not on every number update. Open interest, funding and liquidations come from the Global Asset Data Analytics feeds. On-chain, from Coin Metrics' free community data (daily, where it covers the coin): MVRV is market cap ÷ realized cap (below 1 means holders are underwater on average, above about 3.5 has marked past tops); exchange net flow is coins sent to exchanges minus coins withdrawn, in USD (net withdrawals are usually read as accumulation); active addresses counts addresses that sent or received that day. Glassnode's own metrics need a paid Glassnode API plan, so they aren't used. The summary line is written by fixed rules from these numbers, not by an AI model.
                    Performance & health uses daily candles for the selected coin (Binance or Bybit, then OKX, Coinbase or Kraken). Returns: 24h, 7, 30 and 90 days, 1 year and year to date. Health is the average of up to seven 0–100 factor scores: Trend (price against the 50- and 200-day averages), Momentum (30-day return), Drawdown (distance from the 1-year high), Volatility (30-day, annualized; calmer scores higher), Liquidity (24h volume), Money flow (20-day CMF) and Leverage (funding; crowded funding scores lower). 70 or more reads Healthy, 55–69 Stable, 40–54 Weak and under 40 Stressed. It describes the coin's current condition, not where it goes next.
                    Layer definitions. Swing high / low: a candle whose high (or low) is the extreme of the 4 candles on each side. BOS / CHoCH: a close beyond the last swing level; BOS continues the trend, CHoCH is the first break against it. Fair value gap: a three-candle gap where candle 1 and candle 3 don't overlap; it fades once price fills it. Order block: the last opposite candle before the move that broke structure. Liquidity: two or more swing highs (or lows) within 0.15% of each other. Smart band: the range from the lowest low to the highest high since the latest swing high and swing low; the top half is premium (where SMC traders look to sell), the bottom half is discount (where they look to buy), and the dashed line is the 50% equilibrium. Bollinger 20D: the middle band is a 480-bar simple moving average of hourly closes (24 hours × 20 days), and the upper and lower bands add and subtract 2 × the 480-bar sample standard deviation, following Glassnode's 20-day hourly definition. The width tracks realized volatility over the past 20 days and updates every hour; on every timeframe, each candle uses the band from its last hour. It's calculated here from up to 2,000 hourly exchange candles (Binance or Bybit, then OKX, Coinbase or Kraken), not taken from Glassnode. A Bollinger squeeze means today's band width is in the narrowest 10% of the band widths available (about the last two months); low volatility like this often comes before a large move, but not in a predictable direction. Realized Price (BTC): the average price at which every bitcoin last moved on the blockchain, roughly what all holders paid on average, calculated as realized cap ÷ supply. Delta Price (BTC): (realized cap − average cap) ÷ supply, where average cap is the running average of market cap since July 2010; it has marked past cycle bottoms, so it's often read as an "undervalued" floor. Both are drawn on BTC with the Day, Week and 2 Week timeframes, from Coin Metrics' free community data (CC BY-NC 4.0, daily values). Balanced Price isn't included because no free source publishes the transfer price it needs. London open: shaded 07:00 to 10:00 UTC on 1m, 15m and 1h. The smart read above the chart is written by fixed rules from these same overlays, not by an AI model.
                    How the score works. Each coin gets up to 12 readings, each scaled from −1 to +1, and its momentum is their average × 100. Price (exchange candles, daily): 7-day return (±15% = full scale), 30-day return (±30%), close against its 20-day average (±8%), 14-day RSI (25 points from 50), and volume over the last 3 days against the 30-day average, counted in the direction of the 7-day move. Flow & derivatives (exchanges, live): open interest change over 24 hours in the direction of the 24-hour price move (±10%), Binance taker buy ÷ sell volume over 24 hours (±0.15 from 1), OI-weighted funding (±0.03%) and whale net buying over the last hour from the whale feed. On-chain (Coin Metrics free community data, daily, only where it covers the coin): active addresses over the last 7 days against the 7 days before (±20%), transaction count the same way (±20%), and exchange net flow over 7 days as a share of all exchange flow (withdrawals count as positive). A reading that can't be loaded is left out rather than guessed, and Price, Flow and Chain show "—" when none of their readings loaded. Divergence marks a coin whose price and flow scores point in opposite directions and are at least 60 points apart. The read above the list is written by fixed rules from these scores, not by an AI model. 40 or more reads Strong up, 15 to 39 Up, −14 to 14 Flat, −39 to −15 Down, −40 or less Strong down. Money flow (MFI): the Money Flow Index is a volume-weighted RSI from 0 to 100: it adds up typical price × volume on candles that closed up against those that closed down over the window. 1D uses the last 24 hourly candles; 7D, 30D, 90D and 120D use that many daily candles (Binance spot, or Binance perpetual where there's no spot market; your coins also fall back to Bybit). 80 or more reads overbought, 60–79 buyers in control, 41–59 balanced, 21–40 sellers in control, 20 or less oversold. Health · Perf: the same health score as Performance & health (0–100: Trend, Momentum, Drawdown, Volatility, Liquidity, Money flow and Leverage where funding is known), with 7- and 30-day returns; hover it for every factor, and Details lists them all with 24h, 90-day, 1-year and year-to-date returns. For your coins it uses up to a year of daily candles once Performance & health has scanned them, and otherwise the 130 daily candles Token Momentum loads, so the 200-day average isn't counted until then. Top 100 coins use those 130 candles too. A coin without daily candles shows —. Click 1D, 7D, 30D, 90D or 120D above the column to rank by it; Money flow ranks by MFI 30D. Details also lists Chaikin money flow (20 days), net taker flow (market buys minus market sells, 7 and 30 days, Binance only), raw money flow over 30 days and the on-balance-volume trend. MFI 30D, net taker flow 7D and Chaikin money flow also count toward the Flow score. A coin with less history than a window shows — for it. Sector tags: each coin shows its sector (purple) and ecosystem (blue). For your coins the sector is a fixed, hand-checked label; for the top 100 it's the most specific CoinGecko category the coin belongs to among the 15 largest sectors, and ecosystems come from the 10 largest ecosystems. Details lists every matching CoinGecko category. A coin outside those lists shows "unclassified". The Sector menu filters the list to one sector. Sectors: the Sectors button lists every category CoinGecko publishes (usually 600 or more), in three groups: Sectors, Ecosystems (categories named after a chain's ecosystem) and Other (VC portfolios, stablecoins, wrapped and bridged tokens, launchpads and similar groups that aren't real sectors). Filter them by size or search by name; the list shows 60 at a time. Each one's details add its rank, its share of the whole crypto market cap, volume ÷ market cap and CoinGecko's own description. Sector tags on coins and the stats strip leave Other out, and Hottest sector and Top ecosystem only count groups of $100M or more. Sector flow is the 24-hour change in the group's market cap in dollars — money moving in or out of it, including price moves — and Volume is its 24-hour trading volume. For the 30 largest sectors and 20 largest ecosystems, and any group whose details you open, the dashboard also loads its largest coins (up to 100) to get market-cap-weighted 7- and 30-day changes, breadth (share of coins up over 7 days) and an average 1-day MFI from coins it already tracks. Sector momentum averages the 24-hour change (±5%), 7-day (±15%), 30-day (±30%) and breadth. The stats strip at the top counts the sectors and ecosystems tracked and MFI spikes: coins in your coins or the top 100 whose 1-day MFI is 80 or more (▲ inflow spike) or 20 or less (▼ outflow spike). Arkham's labeled wallet and entity data needs an Arkham API key, so it isn't used. Top 100: switch to see CoinGecko's top 100 coins by market cap (one request, refreshed every 10 minutes). Their score averages the 1-hour (±3%), 24-hour (±10%), 7-day (±25%) and 30-day (±50%) returns, distance from the all-time high (−50% reads as neutral), and funding where Binance or Bybit lists a USDT perpetual. Free on-chain data doesn't cover most of these coins, so they aren't scored on-chain in this list. Stablecoins (priced near $1 with almost no 7- or 30-day change) are left out. The 24h, 7d and 30d buttons rank by that raw price change instead of the score. My coins: your original 23 plus every coin in CoinGecko's top 100 by market cap (stablecoins, wrapped and staked versions of other coins left out), added the first time the top 100 loads and remembered for next time; new top-100 coins are added as they appear. Every coin opens in the chart (the ↗ next to a top-100 coin opens it on CoinGecko instead). A top-100 coin uses the same exchange candles (Binance, then Bybit, then Binance.US); if none of them lists it against USDT, the chart shows NO DATA instead of candles. Added coins are tracked everywhere your 23 are: live prices and whale trades from Binance spot and perpetuals, Bybit and OKX, liquidations, funding, open interest, Token Momentum, Performance & health, Signal Core and the money-flow scans. A coin an exchange doesn't list simply gets no data from that exchange. Global Asset Data Analytics draws at most 50 bubbles (your original 23, the coin in the chart, and the largest added coins); its table lists every coin. Hand-checked sector labels exist only for the original 23; the rest use CoinGecko's categories. Momentum describes the recent move, not where price goes next, and isn't trading advice.
                    How it decides: five indicators each vote on the last closed candle. Supertrend (10, 3) up or down; close above or below the 50-candle EMA; RSI (14) above 55 shows strength, below 45 weakness; MACD (12, 26, 9) histogram above or below zero; volume counts only when it is at least 1.2× its 20-candle average. Volume is added up across exchanges for the same coin and candle — the chart's exchange plus Binance spot and perpetual, Bybit and OKX perpetuals and Coinbase spot, whichever answer and have every one of the last 21 candles — so one venue's quiet or busy hour doesn't decide the vote. Its direction comes from taker flow (market buys minus market sells, from Binance's candles, which publish it): more than 51% bought votes up, more than 51% sold votes down, anything closer is balanced and doesn't vote. Where no taker data is available, the candle's color decides, as before. On-chain context (shown, not voted): the coin's adjusted transfer volume in USD for the latest full day against its previous 30 days, and exchange net flow, from Coin Metrics' free community data, daily and only for coins it covers. Glassnode's equivalents need a paid Glassnode plan, so they aren't used. Realized profit & loss (shown, not voted): net realized P/L is the dollar profit minus loss locked in by coins that moved on-chain that day, valued against the price they last moved at. Without a key it's worked out from Coin Metrics' free daily data as the day's change in realized cap minus the value of newly issued coins, which is the same quantity; it's daily, for the latest full day (not intraday), and only for coins Coin Metrics publishes realized cap for, mainly BTC. Realized profit and realized loss as separate figures (BTC) come from BGeometrics' free bitcoin-data.com feed, which needs no key but allows only 15 requests a day, so the dashboard checks it at most every 8 hours and remembers the result; where both are available, the Coin Metrics figure for the same day is shown as a cross-check. With a Glassnode API key on a plan that includes them, Glassnode's figures are used instead. All of these are daily: the blockchain data behind realized profit and loss is published once per finished day, so there is no free intraday version. Model estimate (every coin, live): for coins without free on-chain figures, and as a live 24-hour reading for all coins, the dashboard estimates realized profit and loss from exchange data. It builds a cost-basis distribution from up to 400 days of daily candles, assuming each day the traded share of supply (volume ÷ circulating supply from CoinGecko) moves to that day's average price; then it treats the volume traded in the last 24 hours of hourly candles as coins sold out of that distribution in proportion, so the part bought below the current price realizes profit and the part above realizes loss. It refreshes every 2 minutes. It uses one exchange's volume (the chart's), and exchange trading isn't the same as coins moving on-chain, so treat it as an estimate of direction and size, not a measured figure; for BTC you can compare it with the on-chain number above it. The key stays in this browser and goes only to Glassnode. The bias is the side with more votes, and confidence is the share of all five that agree with it. The reasoning is written by these rules, not by a machine-learning model, and it isn't trading advice. Adaptive weights: when a new candle closes, the dashboard checks each indicator on this coin and timeframe — how often its vote matched the direction of price 12 candles later. It works out weights from the first 70% of the loaded candles and tests them on the last 30%, which the weights never saw. Adaptive weights are switched on only if they beat equal votes on that test, with at least 20 calls each; otherwise the plain 5-vote count stays. Then the weights are refit on all the candles. An indicator that was right 50% of the time or less gets weight 0. With weights on, the bias is the sign of the weighted average, and confidence is the share of the weight that agrees with it. This is simple statistics recalculated from your candles, not an AI model, and a better past hit rate doesn't guarantee the next call. Live now: every second, the same rules (and the weights, if on) are run on the candle that is still forming. That reading can flip until the candle closes; the big call above uses only closed candles, so it doesn't flicker.
                    The market lean is a weighted average of five readings, each scaled from −1 to +1: MEFI, the money-flow reading (40% BTC spot taker delta over 5 minutes, 30% funding, 30% open-interest change; weight 1), spot taker flow (0.75), the SMC chart's current structure (1), BTC account crowding (0.5, read contrarian) and BTC funding (0.5, also contrarian). +100 means every reading points up. Each tile is a one-line summary; hover it for the full sentence. A green dot means the reading is live, a grey dot that it's still waiting for data: waiting readings show — and are left out of the market lean, which is a MODEL (rule-based) score from live inputs only. Refreshed every 5 seconds; a summary of the panels, not a prediction or trading advice. The market lean and its tiles now sit inside Smart read & brief, in the chart tab. Confluence there checks up to four readings for the selected coin and timeframe: Structure (the latest break of structure), Location (discount counts as bullish, premium as bearish, equilibrium as neutral), Signal Core (only when it is on the same coin) and the market lean (above +25 bullish, below −25 bearish; it is BTC and market-wide, not coin-specific). "Aligned" means all of them, or all but one, point the same way; otherwise it reads Mixed. More agreement doesn't make a move more certain; it only shows the readings aren't contradicting each other. It is worked out by fixed rules, not by an AI model.
                    Chaikin Money Flow (CMF 20) adds up where each of the last 20 candles closed within its range, weighted by volume, from −1 (closing at the lows on heavy volume) to +1 (closing at the highs). Above +0.05 reads as accumulation, below −0.05 as distribution. Taker delta is taker-buy volume minus taker-sell volume from Binance's candles, so it appears only for coins whose candles come from Binance. A divergence means price and money flow pointed opposite ways over those 20 candles. These are inferred from price and volume; they don't see wallets.
                    C3

                    Risk Management

                    Trade setup · entry, stop, target
                    All numbers · size, margin, liquidation, ATR
                      How risk is calculated
                      Auto-calculate plan takes the direction from Signal Core, sets entry at the last closed price, stop loss a chosen multiple of ATR (14) away, and take profit at a chosen multiple of that risk (R). Sizing uses fixed-fraction risk: position size = amount at risk ÷ (stop distance + entry and exit fees). Liquidation is an estimate for an isolated USDT-margined perpetual with 0.5% maintenance margin. Inputs are saved on this computer only. This is a calculator, not trading advice.

                      The 7-step research pipeline

                      MODEL
                      STEP 1—Understand what moves markets

                      How much of each coin's move is just BTC / ETH (beta, R², idiosyncratic vol).

                      STEP 2—Extract signal from noise

                      Rank-IC of momentum, reversal, volume, taker-flow, breakout and low-vol signals vs next-bar returns.

                      STEP 3—Isolate the residual

                      Strip out the BTC factor (trailing beta only) and re-test the signals on what is left.

                      STEP 4—Validate out of sample

                      Walk-forward train → frozen test windows, deflated Sharpe, after fees + slippage.

                      STEP 5—Check the distribution

                      Skew, fat tails, Jarque–Bera, bootstrap Sharpe range, worst days.

                      STEP 6—Manage tail risk

                      Vol targeting, per-coin and gross caps, CVaR, ¼-Kelly cap, drawdown kill-switch.

                      STEP 7—Build a research pipeline

                      Every run saved with settings, sources, look-ahead audit and strategy status.
